distance.note: The DUNE FD TDR Vol. I consistently rounds this to 1300 km; the ProtoDUNE-SP paper gives 1285 km from the neutrino production target to the far detector. The great-circle distance between the two recorded site points is 1288 km.
distance.quote: a far detector located at the 4850 ft level of Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF), in Lead, South Dakota, USA, 1285 km from the neutrino production target

baselines.note: Recorded from the DUNE collaboration’s own publication.

direction.quote: It will also build structures at Fermilab to send neutrinos through stone and earth to South Dakota — no tunnel needed.
direction.value: from Fermilab (Batavia, Illinois) north-west through the Earth to SURF (Lead, South Dakota); no tunnel is required

intervals.label: far-site groundbreaking and construction
intervals.quote: Groundbreaking for the LBNF excavation and construction at Sanford Lab occurred on July 21, 2017.

intervals.label: far-site cavern excavation
intervals.note: Excavation began at the 4850-foot level in 2021 and was reported complete on 1 February 2024.
intervals.quote: Engineering, construction and excavation teams have been working 4,850 feet below the surface since 2021

name: Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility (LBNF) beamline
notes: A dedicated LBNF beam design document could not be fetched in this session; beam parameters come from the DUNE FD TDR Vol. I.

primary_beam.quote: protons, in a wide energy band of 60 GeV to 120 GeV

energy.locator: Vol. I, §1.2 The Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility (LBNF)
energy.quote: the protons, in a wide energy band of 60 GeV to 120 GeV, will collide with a high-power production target

secondary_beam.quote: LBNF will deliver the world’s most intense neutrino beam to the near and far detectors in an on-axis configuration
secondary_beam.value: muon neutrinos / antineutrinos, on-axis, wide band

beam_power.quote: will deliver between 1.0 and 1.2 MW of proton beam power from the Fermilab Main Injector to LBNF

proton_energy.quote: in a wide energy band of 60 GeV to 120 GeV

summary.plain: The facility being built at Fermilab to fire the world’s most intense beam of high-energy neutrinos 1285 kilometres through the Earth to South Dakota, plus the huge caverns that hold the detectors.
summary.technical: On-axis wide-band muon-neutrino beam from 60-120 GeV Main Injector protons, 1.0-1.2 MW initially and upgradable to 2.4 MW, with a 1285 km baseline from Fermilab to the SURF 4850 Level, together with the far-site conventional facilities.

target.note: The TDR calls it a "high-power production target" but the fetched volume does not name the target material.
target.quote: will collide with a high-power production target, creating a secondary beam from which the intense neutrino flux will emerge
